sections.title: The pattern behind jól and rosszul
sections.content: Back when you learned jól ("well") and rosszul ("badly"), you were told the pattern behind them could wait. Here it is: -ul/-ül turns a language name into "in that language" — the regular way Hungarian makes this kind of adverb. Most language names add -ul/-ül directly, following vowel harmony; one you'll meet below needs a linking vowel.

items.english: At home we speak in Hungarian.
How do you say this in English?

sections.content: The vowel follows harmony just like every other suffix you know: back-vowel words take -ul (magyarul, spanyolul), front-vowel words take -ül (németül) — franciául gets a linking á because francia already ends in a vowel.
